clue.text: Representative body starts to deal with something left behind

indicators.note: only the start of the word deal is wanted, its first two letters, with the end dropped

parts.note: the word deal, used as written before it is cut down
a legacy is what a person leaves behind them when they die

explanation.surface: A committee begins dealing with an inheritance someone has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' is plural, so more than one opening letter of 'deal' is taken: its first two.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegacy is a body of delegates, a group appointed to act for others.

clue.text: Kitchen amenity daughter found on coach? Not initially

indicators.note: in a down answer the daughter's letter sits on top of what follows
the coach's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a trainer is a coach

explanation.surface: A useful kitchen item the daughter came across on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus, but it is a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainer is a rack or board where washed dishes are left to drip dry.

clue.text: Books supporter's written about King Edward, truly

indicators.note: the books and the supporter are set down around the king

parts.note: lit is short for literature
an ally is a supporter; the 's is 'is'
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A patron of literature has written about a king, honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally is used as an intensifier meaning actually or really, in fact.

clue.text: Footwear sticks on top of scraper

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above the second

parts.note: to gum something is to stick it down
a hoe is a tool for scraping weeds

explanation.surface: A shoe gets glued to the top of a scraping tool.
explanation.walkthrough: GUMSHOE is mostly met as US slang for a detective, from his soft rubber-soled shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumshoe is a rubber-soled shoe or galosh, worn by sneaking detectives.

clue.text: Exclusive group's simple dwelling overlooking great lake

indicators.note: in a down answer the dwelling stands above the lake

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage or hut
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A select set owns a humble hut with a view over a large lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small close-knit circle of people sharing interests.

clue.text: Hairy-footed midget's pastime, mostly just what's needed

indicators.note: most of the word for a pastime is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a hobby is a pastime
'it' is what something is when it is exactly the thing wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A small hairy-footed creature's hobby turns out to be just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's hobbits are small folk famous for their hairy feet.

clue.text: War on kid initially harming complex creation

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so these letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, read as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of harming is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter supplies one piece of the fodder

explanation.surface: A war on children, first hurting them, is an elaborate thing someone made.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something made by a particular person, their own creation.

clue.text: Prows of vessels steaming in arrow's range

parts.note: a ship's bows are its prow
steaming means very hot

explanation.surface: The front ends of ships puff steam within archery distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowshot is the distance an arrow shot from a bow will travel.

clue.text: The writer's father's books about technique in art

parts.note: the setter's 'I am', shortened
pa is father, plus the 's

indicators.note: the books are turned round

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: The author's dad owns books on artistic method.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting method laying paint on thickly so brush strokes stand out.

clue.text: A university man breaking into a mechanised system

parts.note: taken as written
Tom is a man's name

indicators.note: the words 'into a' are broken up and their letters rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, read as written

explanation.surface: An academic forces his way into some mechanical set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' reads as one phrase for burgling, but 'breaking' is the anagram signal working on 'into a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Automation is the use of machines and control systems to do work without people.

clue.text: Sobbed quietly, kept in by rain

indicators.note: the quiet letter is held inside the word for rain

parts.note: rain is wet weather, and 'the wet' means rainy weather

explanation.surface: Someone cried softly, stuck indoors because of the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry with tears, and sobbed is a matching past tense.

clue.text: Old PM lands with English navy, making spectacular display

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
RN is the Royal Navy
to light on something is to land on it, so lights means lands

explanation.surface: A former prime minister comes ashore with the English fleet in a grand show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lands' looks like a noun for territory but is the verb, as when a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora seen in high northern skies is a famous natural light show.

clue.text: Replace soldiers, as it happens, touring East

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: the word for 'as it happens' goes round the letter for East like a tour circling it

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: Troops are swapped out in real time while travelling around the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace soldiers' reads as one military phrase, but the definition is only 'Replace'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take over their duty or watch, standing in for them.

clue.text: Never, sadly, having capacity to be like Bede!

indicators.note: the letters of never are put in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: the anagram fodder, read as written
to be able is to have the capacity

explanation.surface: Regrettably never able to measure up to the great Bede.
explanation.walkthrough: Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian, always known as the Venerable Bede.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede is his standard title, so venerable is the epithet that describes him.

clue.text: Steps taken to deceive left-wing extremist

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle or trick them
a Trot is a Trotskyist, informally

explanation.surface: Measures adopted to trick a radical of the far left.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxtrot is a ballroom dance, a sequence of set steps.

clue.text: Hit back about woman losing son in gallery

parts.note: re means concerning

indicators.note: the reduced woman goes inside the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: the woman's name drops the letter for son

parts.note: Lisa is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady whose son vanished in an art gallery strikes out in return.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to make a counter-attack, returning a blow or injury.

clue.text: Most senior woman swindled about Japanese currency

indicators.note: the word for swindled is placed around the currency

parts.note: to be done is to be cheated
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: The eldest lady was cheated over a sum in Japanese money.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the senior or most respected female member of a group.

clue.text: Disheartened over a politician's speechmaking

indicators.note: the word over loses its heart, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: the word over, read as written before its middle goes; cricket's O for over is a false lead
taken as written
a Tory is a Conservative politician; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A dispirited Tory politician's address, delivered without enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, especially eloquent speeches.

clue.text: Serious pledge

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a token of what is to come, money paid to seal a deal

explanation.definitionFit: Earnest is both an adjective for being in deadly sincere mood and a noun for a promise-sealing deposit.

clue.text: Early poet's lad catching salmon or sea trout

indicators.note: the lad's word holds the fish inside it, as if he had caught it

parts.note: a son is a lad
a kelt is a salmon or sea trout that has just spawned

explanation.surface: An old poet's boy hooks a fish while out angling.
explanation.walkthrough: John Skelton was a Tudor poet, tutor to the young Henry VIII. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Skelton wrote around 1500, making him one of the earliest named English poets.

clue.text: Freeloader's son, one that smells nasty

parts.note: to pong is British slang for to stink, so a ponger is a stinker

explanation.surface: A scrounger's boy is a smelly character.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off other people's generosity without paying their way.

clue.text: Permanent cross removed from outside

indicators.note: the cross is taken out of the word for outside

parts.note: external means on the outside
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A lasting crucifix has been taken away from the exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, lasting for all time without end.

clue.text: Eating-place's lack of wine, excluding Riesling at first

parts.note: no means a lack of something

indicators.note: the letter that follows is left out

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine

indicators.note: only the first letter of Riesling is taken

parts.note: the German white wine, here just supplying its first letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant with no wine list, not even a Riesling to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSHERY is British slang, from nosh meaning food. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noshery is an informal word for a café or restaurant, a place to get food.

clue.text: A rare, laborious alternative name for 10

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of these letters is wanted

parts.note: the anagram fodder, read as written

explanation.surface: An uncommon, painstaking other name for the northern lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative name' reads as a single phrase, but 'alternative' does double duty as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora borealis is the Latin, scientific name for the northern lights at 10-across.

clue.text: Bird lost height quickly over the pond

definitions.text: lost height quickly over the pond
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in American English '...' is the past tense of dive

explanation.walkthrough: 'over the pond' means across the Atlantic, in America, where dove replaces dived.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove is a bird, and Americans say a diver dove where the British say dived.

clue.text: Plundering gang takes a long time pinching gear

indicators.note: the gang's word grips the gear between its letters, as if stealing it

parts.note: a band is a gang
a rig is a set of equipment
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A gang of thieves spends ages stealing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigandage is robbery by bands of outlaws, the plundering done by brigands.

clue.text: Attempt to stop tree going west — or shrub

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading right to left
the attempt plugs the tree's word like a stopper

parts.note: an elm is a tree
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A bid to halt a tree spreading westward, or else a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Luxury car in outskirts of Derby? That's funny

indicators.note: the car sits inside the outer letters of Derby
only the edges of the word Derby, its first and last letters, are used

parts.note: the English city's name, read as written so its edges can be taken
Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: Spotting a Rolls-Royce on the edge of Derby, someone finds it amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is comic humour, something that is funny in a dry way.
